caption: Our All-Ireland Victory Centennial monument, marking 100 years since Two Mile Borris represented Tipperary and won the 1900 All-Ireland Hurling Final at Jones' Road in Dublin (we beat London 2-5 to 0-6). The names of that winning panel are on the centre plaque, with the club's red-and-yellow flying alongside the Tipperary blue-and-gold. A piece of GAA history that very few villages can match.

Close-up of the names plaque at the heart of the monument. Every member of the 1900 winning panel listed by name: Tom Allen, Watty Dunne, Bill Gleeson, Billy Gleeson, Jack Gleeson, John Hackett, Ned Hackett, Ned Hayes (Captain), Paddy Hayes, Tom Healy, Tom Kennedy, Jack Leahy, Pat Lonergan, Billy Maher, Charlie Maher, Denis Maher, Jack Maher, Mikey Maher, Ned Maher, Paddy Maher (Best), James Meaney, James Morris, Jim O'Keeffe, John Purcell, Matt Purcell, Mick Purcell, Matty Ryan, Tom Ryan, Tommy Ryan, Paddy Stapleton, Tom Semple, Mickey Treacy, Mike Wall, Johnny Walsh and Tom Whelan. The Irish inscription at the bottom dedicates the monument to the glory of God and the honour of Two-Mile-Borris (May 2026)

The smaller plaque on the cobbles at the foot of the monument: unveiled on 26th August 2000 by Sean McCague, then President of the GAA, and blessed by Most Rev. Dermot Clifford, Archbishop of Cashel and Emly. Erected by Jerome Lennon for Stone Developments Ltd, Carlow (May 2026)

Our Mutt Mitt dispenser at the monument area. The 2025 adjudicator found this empty when they called in, so we've kept it on the volunteer round and Cllr Sean Ryan has offered to pull a stockpile down from Clonmel for us (May 2026)

A planting day at the monument area, getting the wooden raised bed filled in with split perennials from our other beds. Locally-made wooden raised beds are part of our cohesive village-wide planter scheme.
The All-Ireland Victory Centennial monument surrounded by colourful Poppies, Salvia, Lamb's Ear and Hebe (May 2026)

The main flower bed at the village centre absolutely packed with colour! Red Poppies, pink Phlox, yellow Wallflowers, purple Salvia, blue Lobelia and clipped Box and Hebe shrubs. A fantastic display of year-round structure with gorgeous seasonal colour right at the heart of Two-Mile-Borris (May 2026)
Arabis, Heuchera and Hebe looking well at the Community Garden sign (May 2026)
Hebes, Foxgloves, Anemone and Catmint looking lovely at the Monk (June 2025)
Fantastic display of Poppies, Lamb's Ear, Salvia, Wallflowers, Phlox and Hebe in the main flower bed (May 2026)
Volunteer-maintained Alliums and naturalised wildflowers along the main road heading west, just before you reach the monument area. A lovely soft welcome into the heart of the village (May 2026)

Our Christmas lights switch-on parade, with decorated tractors rolling down the main street under the lit-up canopy. The whole village turns out for this every year, and between the singers, the pipers, the mulled wine and Santa coming in on the lead tractor it's a brilliant night (December 2023)
